test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A field is in the shape of a rhombus, whose perimeter is 292 m and one of its diagonals is 96 m. What is the area of the field?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Side** of the **rhombus** = 292 ÷ 4 = 73 m.

The diagonals of a **rhombus** bisect each other at 90°. Using the **Pythagorean triplet** (48, 55, 73):

Half of the second **diagonal** = √(73² − 48²) = √(5329 − 2304) = √3025 = 55 m.

Full second **diagonal** (d₂) = 55 × 2 = 110 m.

**Area** = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = (1/2) × 96 × 110 = 48 × 110 = 5280 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 5280 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** of the rhombus = 292 m, **Diagonal 1 (d₁)** = 96 m.

**Formula Used:** **Area** of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂; 4 × (**side**)² = d₁² + d₂².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2365d77da3cefebad59b5c80ac28a803869ccaa9c97fcde0cabdd0e3e3387d1.png] 

⇒ **Side** of **rhombus** (a) = Perimeter / 4 = 292 / 4 = 73 m.

⇒ In right-angled triangle ABE (where E is the intersection of diagonals):

⇒ AE² + EB² = AB²

⇒ AE² + (96/2)² = 73²

⇒ AE² + 48² = 5329

⇒ AE² = 5329 − 2304 = 3025

⇒ AE = √3025 = 55 m.

⇒ Second **diagonal** (d₂) = 2 × AE = 2 × 55 = 110 m.

⇒ **Area** of the field = (1/2) × 96 × 110

⇒ **Area** = 48 × 110 = 5280 m².

Thus, the correct option is (3).

**∴ The correct answer is 5280 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All sides are equal, and diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°). The relationship between sides and diagonals is 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Area using Trigonometry

The area of a rhombus can also be calculated if a side (a) and an interior angle (θ) are known: Area = a² × sin(θ).

Pythagorean Triplets in Rhombus

Frequent triplets in rhombus problems include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (20, 21, 29), and (48, 55, 73).</p
